reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin and OneExchange as a profit-oriented trading and mining opportunity, linking package purchases and paid-partner status to exchange access and describing token sales and partner invitations as ways to recover costs and get faster results. It also promotes token doubling, projected price growth, future Bitcoin-like utility, and possible profit. The speaker acknowledges risk and no guarantee, and the available video evidence does not establish actual operation, purchases, returns, or losses.

citations.quote: You entered the 1000 euro package, you have 10 thousand tokens
use the remaining tokens for mining
Tokens bought on the stock market freeze for 30 days
everything doubles
it will be nice to see twice as many tokens in my office

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly treats the activity as a market subject to uncertainty, not as a guaranteed-income scheme. The speaker expressly says participation is a personal choice and that each person bears the risk. He also acknowledges that the token price can fall and that there is no guarantee, while explaining that price behavior depends on market conditions. Those are material risk disclosures, not assurances that viewers will profit. The slide itself also presents the possibility of price movement in either direction. A cautious explanation of a speculative asset, including its risks and mechanics, is more consistent with financial commentary than deceptive certification of a safe investment.

citations.quote: it's your personal choice, of course, everyone takes all the risk for himself
Yes, the token's price can fall like any other asset
no guarantee is no gives because this is a market

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes optimistic language while minimizing the warnings that qualify it. A discussion of token splits, future uses, or possible profit does not itself establish deception when the speaker expressly says prices can fall and gives no guarantee. The cited package and mining references show the subject being discussed, but do not show that viewers were promised a return, pressured to buy, or told losses were impossible.

citations.quote: no guarantee is no gives because this is a market
can make their own decisions

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not erase the presentation's central inducement. The speaker still describes a strategy for recovering the original funds and retaining additional tokens, while framing doubling and future appreciation as attractive outcomes. The warning that prices may fall is a generic qualification; it does not show that the underlying claims about token quantity, mining, or future value are substantiated. A disclaimer can accompany a solicitation without changing its commercial purpose.

opening.argument: The material is structured as a school-style operational lesson about using an exchange. It explains order status, trading hours, minimum transaction size, token freezes, commissions, passwords, and the sections of the platform. The speaker repeatedly frames the session as instruction, including recommending academy materials so participants can learn before trading. Explaining how an interface and its rules are supposed to work is not the same as proving that the asset will appreciate or soliciting a particular purchase. The focus on procedures and platform functions supports an educational and technology-demonstration interpretation.

citations.quote: OneCoin School for Trading on the OneExchange
Tomorrow on Monday we all will have the opportunity to check again how the exchange actually works, in real-time
we recommend everyone to learn the materials of 1Academy Academy
The order can be opened, not yet executed, closed

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats every financial topic in an instructional lesson as an investment pitch. But the cited mechanics are precisely what a tutorial would explain: how orders operate, how tokens are traded, and what users can observe. Future-oriented examples appear within that lesson and are not proof that the entire presentation is a deceptive offer. The excerpts do not establish that the speaker represented the tutorial as a guaranteed result.

citations.quote: The order can be opened, not yet executed, closed
According to the contract, the order is operating five working days

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional form does not determine substance. The lesson explains how to participate in a system while also presenting purchased tokens, mining, partner recruitment, and projected growth as ways to make money. The exchange tutorial therefore functions as operational support for the promoted opportunity, not neutral technology education. The title and interface explanations do not substantiate the promised future utility or returns.

citations.quote: simulate using the tools that the company gives and choose an investment strategy
we can make a good profit from it
We can sell a package using the recommendation

opening.argument: At most, the evidence describes a proposed commercial platform offering tokens and exchange-related services. The mechanics include an ordinary minimum transaction, order cancellation, operating periods, and a financial password. The material also expressly limits what the token can do: it may be bought or sold, but it cannot be transferred directly to another partner. Most importantly, the supplied evidence does not show a guaranteed return, an actual payout, a credential request, or a completed loss. It describes a product and its proposed trading rules, with risks openly acknowledged. That supports treating it as ordinary commerce or a service demonstration rather than labeling the presentation itself a scam.

citations.quote: The minimum size is only 50 tokens
no guarantee is no gives because this is a market
We can sell a package using the recommendation

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from the commercial subject matter instead of identifying a deceptive mechanism. A package, token sale, or referral can be part of a business promotion without proving that the promoter guaranteed returns or concealed risk. The speaker says participants make their own decisions, and the materials acknowledge both price declines and the absence of guarantees. The evidence therefore supports a regulated-risk commerce framing at least as well as the accusation.

citations.quote: no one should drive anyone away
Yes, the token's price can fall like any other asset
no guarantee is no gives because this is a market

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing elements are not enough to make the promotion ordinary commerce. The presentation links packages, paid-partner access, token quantity increases, mining, and partner recommendations to recovering funds and earning more. It also displays a forecast that projects substantial future prices and describes the exchange as a way to make profit. The absence of a completed payout or explicit credential request says only that the evidence is promotional, not that its solicitation is benign.
